comment: RI-TEC-017 fits. A rulebook sets legal obligations, while RI-TEC-020 concerns compliance in practice; the source reports no compliance failure.
Checked in source: the law is the Law on Electronic Documents, Electronic Identification and Trust Services, so RI-TEC-025 holds.
Exception LIM-0019 is cited in the extraction note.

An electronic filing system for asset statements; the assignment note itself says interoperability is not stated. RI-TEC-028 rests only on the link to the recommendation at MKD-EU-2023-003-0055. Better queued for the analyst.
"Most countries" does not name North Macedonia, as the note accepts, so the item says nothing about the issue in this country. The sentence is otherwise on topic.
Checked in source: the next sentences concern personal data misuse in fast loans, so RI-TEC-020 holds.
Concerns connection to the interoperability platform (INT-MKD-0128), so implementation is at least as good a fit as unresolved_gap.
RI-TEC-023 fits the degree programmes for cybersecurity professionals, but less well the safe internet content in primary curricula, which is close to digital skills (R2). No better issue exists.

Chapter 27 chemicals databases: IT security is the subject, but this is a sector system neither connecting to an EU system nor used by the public, which extraction rules section 4 puts out by default. The cybersecurity theme gives the case for keeping it.
Non-EU finding on how the named national e-services portal (INT-MKD-0124) is used; rules section 1 gives implementation. RI-TEC-003 stands.
Checked in source: the system is the Employment Service Agency IT system, so RI-FMW-005 holds.
Mentions digital skills, but the claim also concerns digitalisation of the economy and business competitiveness, so RI-TEC-033 holds.
Checked in source: action A.3.2.14.1 is led by the Public Revenue Office, consistent with RI-TEC-005 as limited at G4.
Checked in source: the Directive is the Law Enforcement Directive and the amending law concerns the Agency's independence, so both issues hold.

Digital health section, but the claim is about engaging the ICT innovation ecosystem to regain competitiveness on an index. RI-TEC-009 covers interoperability, paper referrals and legislation, none stated here. Alternative is queued_unmatched.
Follows the default for EU sources, but flagged reported_view: the country describes its own use of e-catalogues, not an EU requirement.
The quote blames lack of hardware, connections and licences, so institutions cannot use the system rather than choosing not to; MEC-11 assumes a system that works and goes unused. RI-TEC-004 stands.
Same point as MKD-GOV-2026-002-0007: adoption of a rulebook is the legal framework, not compliance in practice.
Concerns statistics from the national portal (INT-MKD-0124) as well as institutions' portals, so implementation is at least as good a fit as unresolved_gap.
Non-EU finding on ticket handling for the named national e-services portal (INT-MKD-0124); rules section 1 gives implementation. RI-TEC-003 stands.
Non-EU finding on how the named interoperability platform (INT-MKD-0128) is applied, namely no security checks on connected systems; rules section 1 gives implementation. Issues stand.
The quote states the law is not fully aligned with the NIS2 Directive, which supports MEC-01 directly; comparable items (MKD-GOV-2024-001-0013, MKD-EU-2023-003-0073) carry it. RI-TEC-022 stands.

Regional passage on foreign workers generally. RI-FMW-002 is defined by EU workers, and MKD-EU-2025-003-0010 says quotas do not apply to EU citizens. Chapter 2 scope is met, but the issue fit is weak, as the note signals.
Follows the default for EU sources, but this is the country stating what its own law says (reported_view), not an EU requirement or finding. No classification note records a departure.
Electronic filing with one agency, not the national portal; the note calls it closest fit and says it could not clearly be assigned. Rules section 2 uses queued_unmatched when no approved issue fits.
The finding half of the sentence is separately extracted as -0124.
Follows the default for EU sources, but the country is saying what it needs (reported_view), not the Commission setting a requirement. RI-TEC-010 stands.
Internet use rather than coverage; RI-TEC-013 is the closest fit.

e-Rabota is the employment agency portal, not the national e-services portal named in RI-TEC-003, as the note accepts. A transactional service, so the reading is defensible, but it should be visible to the analyst.
